items.title: NST Leader: Mental health support for teachers
items.summary: The Education Ministry has flagged 691 teachers out of 82,126 scanned across primary and secondary schools as needing urgent mental health care and psychological intervention. There are three worrying reasons for the teachers' poor mental health. Finally, 23 teachers categorised as "low" experienced psychological distress, burnout and clinical depression so severe that they can't live and work healthily.

items.title: Families claim Malaysians held in Taiwan were exploited by scam syndicate
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Three Malaysians detained in Taiwan on suspicion of involvement in fraud activities may have been victims of exploitation by the syndicate, says the Malaysian International Humanitarian Organisation (MHO). Its secretary-general, Datuk Hishamuddin Hashim, said the claim was based on information and evidence provided by the families of the individuals concerned. Hishamuddin said MHO believed all information should be thoroughly examined to ensure the circumstances faced by each individual were assessed fairly.

items.title: Tuan Ibrahim: CSA must not become political bargaining chip
items.summary: PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the opposition coalition believed that supporting the Budget and government bills was enough, without having to enter into a formal agreement with the government. Tuan Ibrahim said opposition MPs had continued to support the Budget and various bills tabled by the government, except for the proposed legislation to limit the prime minister's tenure. He added that even the proposed legislation had not received unanimous support from government MPs.

items.title: Zahid hopes Malaysia-China ties will continue to strengthen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes Malaysia-China relations will continue to strengthen through closer cooperation that benefits both countries. Earlier today, Zahid received a delegation at the Malaysia-China Friendship Dinner in Putrajaya, which provided a platform for both sides to exchange views and share the latest developments. He said the meeting also provided an opportunity to continue discussions following his recent official working visit to Beijing and Tianjin.

items.title: Sim: Local businesses must benefit from government, GLC and MNC procurement
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The government wants local content to be given greater consideration in procurement by government agencies, government-linked companies (GLCs) and multinational corporations (MNCs) to create more opportunities for local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim said the approach was aimed at ensuring local businesses benefited from investments and the development of domestic supply chains. So, there must be a requirement for local content," he said.

items.title: Macron's Malaysia visit set to boost bilateral ties
items.summary: Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said Macron is expected to visit Malaysia from Nov 16-17. Sim said the visit would provide fresh impetus for collaboration between Malaysian and French companies, building on decades of commercial relations and growing investment ties. Sim said Malaysia and France have enjoyed more than 350 years of trade ties.

items.title: Melaka polls: Gen Z wants swift action, solutions – Adly
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan Melaka chairman Adly Zahari has defended the coalition's young candidate for the Kuala Linggi state seat, Mohammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah. Adly said Muklis Mubin and PH's Klebang candidate Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir, 26, were among the young faces fielded by the coalition in the Melaka state election. He said Muklis Mubin had been an active volunteer and was entitled to help the public by working with relevant agencies.

items.title: BYD, Gentari eye Petronas stations for flash charging
items.summary: BYD and Gentari are exploring the deployment of ultra-fast EV charging infrastructure in Malaysia, including at Petronas stations and major highway corridors, as the Chinese automaker seeks to expand charging options for its vehicles. BYD Malaysia and Gentari recently signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) at BYD's global headquarters in Shenzhen to explore bringing BYD flash charging technology to Malaysia, although a rollout timeline and investment details were not disclosed. Existing BYD models can also use the charging infrastructure, but charging speeds will depend on each vehicle's capabilities.

items.title: Melaka polls: MCA gets two additional seats based on winnability – Rauf
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional have allocated two additional seats to MCA for the Melaka election based on winnability and ground assessments, said state BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh. The latest allocation brings MCA's total to four seats, while BN will contest 23 seats overall. "Both sides agreed to hand the seats to MCA.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Friday, Oct 30, 2026

items.title: Vandalism caused broken window on KTM Komuter train, says KTMB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A broken window on the Padang Besar-Butterworth KTM Komuter Utara service, which went viral on social media yesterday, was caused by vandalism, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has confirmed. In a statement today, KTMB said Train No. KTMB said it had lodged a police report.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 30, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Anwar orders train fix Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has directed Transport Minister Anthony Loke and Rapid KL to address recurring train congestion affecting commuters. 2015 assault complaint revived Lawyers for a former policeman say he is seeking justice by reviving an 11-year-old assault complaint against former senior police officer Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain. MCA gains fourth seat MCA will contest four seats in the Melaka election after securing Kota Laksamana from Perikatan Nasional, bringing Barisan Nasional's allocation to 23 seats.

items.title: i‑City's newest residences powered by Nvidia
items.summary: Called i-Ris, the digital assistant will use Nvidia's digital-human technology and computing capabilities to help residents interact with their homes and coordinate connected services. TwinMatrix, an Nvidia Inception company, will use Nvidia ACE technology to develop a lifelike digital avatar designed to communicate naturally with residents. Nvidia's graphics processing unit computing will support the AI systems that link different home technologies.

items.title: Lianson adds Malaysia's first DP2 heavy-lift vessel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lianson Fleet Group Bhd (LFG) is expanding its offshore marine capabilities with the acquisition of a heavy-lift vessel capable of handling up to 4,000 tonnes. This positions the group to pursue larger and more complex offshore projects across Southeast Asia. He said the vessel would complement Lianson's existing fleet ownership, chartering and offshore support operations, allowing it to pursue larger projects across the offshore energy lifecycle.

items.title: Malaysian doctor Mary Suma Cardosa makes history as first Asian to lead global pain research body
items.summary: In a statement issued by IASP, she said her presidency would focus on advancing pain science, strengthening healthcare education and improving access to effective pain management worldwide. “Pain affects people in every country, but access to effective pain care remains profoundly unequal,” she said, highlighting the importance of education, stronger clinical services and multidisciplinary cooperation. An anaesthesiologist with more than three decades of experience in pain medicine, Cardosa has played a pivotal role in developing Malaysia’s pain management services and strengthening pain education in the country and across Southeast Asia.

items.title: Ni Hsin links treasury share sale to stock volatility
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ni Hsin Group Bhd says the resale of five million treasury shares for RM2.38 million may have contributed to the sharp fall in its share price and surge in trading volume. In its response to Bursa Malaysia's unusual market activity (UMA) query today, the cookware manufacturer said it could not conclusively establish whether the disposal had triggered the recent trading activity. The shares were resold on Oct 26 at between 47.5 sen and 48 sen apiece, leaving the company with 44.35 million treasury shares.

items.title: Nepal floods: Perkeso payments to next of kin expected on Nov 4 – MASFIH
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) payments to the next of kin of Malaysians who perished in the Nepal-Tibet flood tragedy are expected to be disbursed on Nov 4, according to Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH). MASFIH coordinator and spokesperson Dr Manivannan Rethinam said several families had been informed of the development by Perkeso, which was expediting the collection of supporting documents to facilitate the payments. Manivannan said MASFIH had also helped facilitate the process by coordinating contact details of the next of kin after highlighting several communication challenges at the initial stage.

items.title: Ab Rauf earns UKM doctorate with research on digital village initiative
items.summary: MELAKA: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has completed his Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) through Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's (UKM) Accreditation of Prior Experiential Learning for Qualifications (APEL.Q) programme after 2 years of study. He said his research, titled Digital Technology Management Among Traditional Village Communities: An Analysis of the Melaka Digital Village Initiative, focused on efforts to harness digital technology among traditional village communities to help them navigate the digital transformation. This is not merely a personal accomplishment, but a tribute to Melaka and my commitment to continuing to strengthen the Digital Village initiative for the people's future," he said.

items.title: Bank Rakyat names fintech accelerator winners
items.summary: The programme is organised in collaboration with PlugAndPlay and the Fintech Association of Malaysia (FAOM), with support from Payments Network Malaysia Sdn Bhd (PayNet). TNEX Malaysia Sdn Bhd won the grand award, while Unbraided AI Sdn Bhd received the silver award and Carbon AI Sdn Bhd the bronze award. The other participants were PowerCred Technologies, Dataverse Sdn Bhd, Finology Sdn Bhd, IntelliLabs AI Solution, Codebase Technologies, GBG (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, Vespid Sdn Bhd and Wazzap Me Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Paws off! Shah Alam High Court rules condo management cannot impose blanket pet bans
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 30 — The High Court here today ruled that a joint management body (JMB) cannot impose a blanket ban on keeping pets in private residential units through its house rules. They said the court ruled that the mere presence of pets in a residential unit did not constitute a breach of house rules and that any enforcement action must be based on By-law 14 of the Strata Management (Maintenance and Management) Regulations 2015 and supported by evidence. House Rule 9.0 cannot be used to prohibit or penalise Ms Noraseela merely for keeping her three cats; Enforcement must be evidence-based.

items.title: MAA Group faces going concern warning after RM107mil loss
items.summary: This follows a RM106.9 million loss in its financial year 2026 (FY26), the group said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today. MAA said it received an unqualified audit opinion with a material uncertainty related to going concern for the financial year ended June 30, 2026. However, the going concern warning highlights uncertainty over the group's financial position.

items.title: Melaka polls: Clear skies expected on nomination morning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Clear skies are expected across all three districts in Melaka tomorrow morning, coinciding with nomination day for the state election. According to the Malaysian Meteorological Department's (MetMalaysia) website, Jasin, Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah are expected to experience clear weather in the morning, with temperatures ranging from 23 to 24 degrees Celsius. The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day tomorrow and early voting on Nov 10.

items.title: Forest fires affect five Indonesian provinces, floods hit thousands in North Sumatra
items.summary: JAKARTA: Forest and land fires have affected 1,410 hectares across five Indonesian provinces, while floods have displaced or affected thousands of households in North Sumatra, prompting continued disaster response operations across the country. It was followed by Central Sulawesi with 295 hectares, Southeast Sulawesi (257 hectares), Maluku (182 hectares) and East Kalimantan (174 hectares). Separately, Berton said floods in North Sumatra had affected 7,615 households.

items.title: RM3 for extra soup? Labuan eatery compounded for failing to display charge on menu
items.summary: LABUAN, Oct 30 — An eatery operator here was compounded after charging an additional RM3 for a serving of soup that was not listed on the restaurant’s displayed price menu. KPDN Labuan director Junaidah Arbain said the action followed a consumer complaint lodged through the ministry’s e-Aduan portal, with an inspection at about 10am finding that the displayed price list included additional charges for rice and noodles but did not specify the price of extra soup. “Following the non-compliance detected, we issued a compound to the operator under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering (Price Marking for Goods and Charges for Services) Order 2020, under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011,” she told Bernama today.

items.title: Foreign investments should deliver more opportunities for Malaysian SMEs, says Steven Sim
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — The government wants local content to be given greater consideration in government, government-linked company (GLC) and multinational corporation (MNC) procurements to create more opportunities for local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). “We also want government procurements, GLC procurements and, of course, MNC procurements to have a perspective for local content. So, there must be a requirement for local contents,” he said.

items.title: Brickfields' Little India comes alive ahead of Deepavali
items.summary: Footwear and accessories trader Vishan Daren, 30, said recent rain had reduced footfall and affected his sales. However, he said demand for festive essentials had picked up today, and he expected more customers on Saturday and Sunday. Usha said Deepavali also attracted customers from other communities interested in Indian traditional wear, reflecting the cultural diversity of the celebration.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH raises target to contest 24 seats, eyes 18 wins
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Pakatan Harapan is targeting to win 18 of the 24 state seats it will contest in the Melaka election on Nov 14. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the decision to increase the number of seats from 21 to 24 was made after assessing current political developments and the coalition's ability to field suitable candidates. "We eventually decided to contest 24 state seats," he told a press conference after a PH Hi-Tea with the Melaka Media Practitioners Club (Pendika).

items.title: Zetrix AI's RM2bil sukuk rating slashed to near-default category
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has slashed its rating on Zetrix AI Bhd's RM2 billion Islamic medium-term notes to CIS from BB+IS, citing an unresolved covenant breach, mounting financial claims and worsening governance concerns. The rating remains on MARCWatch Negative, signalling heightened uncertainty over the group's ability to meet its financial obligations and resolve the issues surrounding thd RM2 billion sukuk. The rating agency also flagged mounting pressure on the group's liquidity amid growing financial claims.

items.title: 112 rural projects face RM259.5mil payment arrears
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Outstanding payments to contractors and compensation to landowners totalling RM259.503 million for 112 projects remained unpaid as of Sept 30, said Umno Youth executive council member Fadzmel Fadzil. Dismissing claims that the Rural and Regional Development Ministry had overcommitted financially, Fadzmel said the arrears stemmed from previous years and were not the result of new spending commitments. He said a Finance Ministry (MoF) letter dated Sept 10 had directed spending control measures, including the postponement of allocations that were approved.

items.title: Sarawak doubles Unimas medical intake to produce more local doctors
items.summary: KUCHING: Sarawak will double the intake of new medical students at Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (UNIMAS) from 40 to 80 as part of efforts to produce more local doctors and address the state's shortage of medical personnel. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg said the move was part of the state government's long-term efforts to address a shortfall of more than 1,000 doctors. The state government would prioritise the enrolment of Sarawakians through Yayasan Sarawak sponsorship to ensure more local students had the opportunity to pursue medical studies, he said.

items.title: Malakoff files RM700mil green sukuk for Melaka WTE plant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malakoff Corp Bhd has lodged a RM700 million green sukuk programme to part-finance the development of a waste-to-energy (WTE) facility in Sungai Udang, Melaka scheduled for completion in 2029. Its subsidiary Sungai Udang WTE Sdn Bhd, lodged the 30-year Asean Green Sustainable and Responsible Investment sukuk Wakalah with the Securities Commission. Sungai Udang WTE is 60 per cent owned by Malakoff, while the remaining 40 per cent is held by Alam Flora Environmental Solutions Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Alam Flora Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Ringgit extends rally against US dollar as traders reassess Fed rate hike prospects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit extended its gains to close higher against the US dollar on Friday as traders reassessed the possibility of an interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve (Fed), an analyst said. The Fed decided to keep the benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75 per cent to 4.00 per cent on Oct 28. At 6pm, the ringgit rose to 4.0555/0600 against the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0575/0620.

items.title: IGB Reit's Q3 net profit rises to RM144.15mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IGB Real Estate Investment Trust (IGB Reit) posted a higher net profit of RM144.15 million for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026), from RM95.62 million in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue rose to RM249.33 million from RM165.19 million in Q2 2026. For the cumulative nine months ended Sept 30, 2026 (9M 2026), IGB Reit's net profit increased to RM446.23 million from RM294.70 million, and the revenue also grew to RM751.62 million from RM496.72 million in the previous corresponding period.

items.title: Cathay Pacific says 53,000 bookings affected by unauthorised data access
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: About 53,000 Cathay Pacific bookings are affected by unauthorised access to passenger reservation data held by its third-party technology provider Amadeus. "In the majority of cases, the information accessed included booking reference, passenger name and flight details," Cathay Pacific said in a statement today. Cathay Pacific said there was no evidence that financial or payment information was accessed.

items.title: Eleventh-hour boost for MCA: Perikatan returns Kota Laksamana, bringing Melaka seat tally to four
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — MCA has announced that it will contest one more state seat in the 16th Melaka state election, after Kota Laksamana was returned to Barisan Nasional (BN) by Perikatan Nasional (PN). MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong said Melvin Chua will be fielded as the candidate, following discussions between BN and PN after the latter indicated that MCA is better suited to contest the seat. The addition of Kota Laksamana means MCA will contest four seats, including Machap Jaya, Kelebang and Bandar Hilir.

items.title: Sabah defence upgrades not a response to Philippine military build-up, says Khaled
items.summary: LABUAN, Oct 30 — Malaysia will continue strengthening its military capabilities in Sabah to safeguard national security amid regional geopolitical developments, but the move is not a direct response to the Philippines’ military build-up on Balabac Island, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. “Every country has the right to strengthen its military capabilities, and Malaysia will do the same. Khaled said strengthening Malaysia’s defence capabilities, particularly in Sabah, remained a key priority of the Defence Ministry.

items.title: The more, the merrier? State Pakatan chairman says crowded Melaka races could work in coalition’s favour
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) does not regard multi-cornered contests in the Melaka state election as a disadvantage, saying a crowded field could instead create more opportunities for the coalition to secure victories. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said a straight fight did not necessarily give a party an advantage, as three- or four-cornered contests could, in certain circumstances, offer better prospects from a strategic standpoint. Also present was Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim.

items.title: MOF never ordered rural road projects cancelled, only deferred new contracts, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The Finance Ministry (MOF) has never issued any directive to cancel rural road projects, but has only deferred new contracts to prevent outstanding payments to contractors from continuing to accumulate, according to the prime minister’s senior political adviser, Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz. He said the deferment was necessary following rural road development expenditure exceeding the original allocations approved by Parliament annually since 2022, resulting in increased contractual commitments and outstanding payments to contractors. “In Sabah and Sarawak alone, actual rural road expenditure this year reached RM1.41 billion, the highest in the past 10 years.

items.title: Saris, sweets and shopping sprees: Deepavali buzz builds across Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The festive atmosphere ahead of Deepavali on November 8 is becoming more vibrant as the Indian community nationwide begins making preparations for the Festival of Lights, including purchasing traditional attire, preparing special delicacies and decorating their homes to celebrate the occasion with family and relatives. Another visitor, N. Rama Rao, 38, said Little India remains his family’s preferred shopping destination as it offers a wide selection of traditional attire at reasonable prices. Shoppers browse traditional attire, accessories and festive decorations ahead of Deepavali in Johor Bahru October 30, 2026.

items.title: Rubbish raid! Thirteen-foot crocodile caught after rummaging through trash for food in Sarawak village
items.summary: KOTA SAMARAHAN, Oct 30 — A crocodile measuring over 13 feet (about 3.96m) was captured this morning following reports of the reptile roaming in the area and posing a potential safety concern for nearby villagers. Licensed crocodile capture team Sarawak Crocter said in a Facebook post that the operation was carried out in collaboration with the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC). — The Borneo Post

items.title: Bought one thing, got another? Anwar orders crackdown on online shopping scams, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), to take immediate action against fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the directive followed Anwar’s concerns over problems faced by online shoppers and sellers, including high commission fees imposed on merchants and customers receiving products that did not match their orders. “The prime minister raised concerns about the problems faced by e-commerce users, particularly high fees and commissions charged to sellers, as well as customers receiving products that differ from what they ordered.

items.title: Repairs on Kuching’s Jalan Lapangan Terbang water main completed, supply restoration in stages, says Sarawak Water
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 30 — Emergency repair works on a critical 750mm mild steel cement-lined (MSCL) water main on Jalan Lapangan Terbang were completed at 2am today, said Sarawak Water Sdn Bhd. The utility provider said water supply restoration is now underway in stages. Following completion of the repair works at 2am, Sarawak Water said valve reopening and network pressurisation had commenced, with water supply expected to be restored gradually.

items.title: Sale of first industrial plots on Silicon Island to start in Q1 2027, says Penang CM
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — The Penang government hopes to sell the first industrial plots on Silicon Island as early as the first quarter of 2027, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the development on Silicon Island will focus on the 700-acre Green Tech Park which is planned as a green, smart and sustainable high-tech industrial hub in line with environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles. He said the first factory in the Green Tech Park is expected to begin operations by 2028 while creating high-skilled employment opportunities for Penangites.

items.title: Indonesian woman fined RM4,000 and ordered deported over RM100 sex offer to undercover cop in Kuching
items.summary: Magistrate Nureina Syafika Mohd Najib imposed the sentence against Pita, 37, after she pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 372B of the Penal Code. During the inspection of an unnumbered room, police found Pita with the undercover agent and arrested her for further action. Investigations found that Pita had offered sexual services to the undercover agent for a cash payment of RM100.

items.title: Penang Budget 2027 sets aside RM600 aid for e-hailing drivers, RM500 for newlyweds
items.summary: “This is for eligible drivers in 2027 with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million,” he said when tabling the Supply Bill at the state legislative assembly today. He said the state government had disbursed RM57.8 million through the implementation of the first and second phases of the i-Sejahtera programme as at September 30. “As such, in 2027, the Penang State Housing Board (LPNPP) will explore the co-living concept for suitable state government rental housing and People’s Housing Programme units,” he said.

items.title: Cabinet agrees to amend guidelines to speed up abandoned vehicle disposal, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Cabinet has agreed to amend the guidelines on the management of abandoned vehicles to speed up the process of removing and disposing of such vehicles, following complaints over delays and poor coordination among enforcement agencies. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposed amendments were put forward by the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) and Transport Ministry (MoT) after taking into account various feedback and complaints about the existing procedures. He said the current process could take too long and required better coordination among the agencies involved.

items.title: Penang tables RM1.07b Budget 2027 with record-low RM5.62m deficit
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow today tabled a RM1.074 billion budget for 2027, with a projected deficit of RM5.62 million. He said the estimated deficit was the lowest in the state’s budget history, compared to the projected deficit of RM19.92 million for 2026. He said the budget included a contribution of RM240 million to the state development fund, compared to RM265 million in 2026.

items.title: Two Penampang road upgrades worth RM173m running ahead of schedule, says Ewon
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Oct 30 — Two rural road upgrade projects in Kampung Buayan and Kampung Terian here, involving a total allocation of RM173.263 million, are making positive progress, with both projects ahead of their scheduled completion timelines. Sabah deputy chief minister III Datuk Ewon Benedick said the RM73.868 million Kampung Buayan rural road upgrade — involving a 5.6-kilometre stretch of road and the construction of two bridges — is at 76.64 per cent physical progress, 45 days ahead of schedule, and is expected to be completed in August 2027, while the RM99.395 million Kampung Terian rural road upgrade — involves a 6.7-kilometre stretch of road — is at 57.83 per cent progress, 58 days ahead of schedule, and is expected to be completed in May 2028. He hoped that both rural road projects, together with other small-scale development projects, would improve infrastructure facilities and benefit residents and visitors to nearby villages once fully completed.

items.title: Govt to begin declassifying historical documents under Official Secrets Act, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The government is expected to declassify historical documents, particularly those classified as official secrets under the Official Secrets Act, as soon as possible, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim raised the matter during the second 2026 National Historians Council meeting held earlier this week. “The Cabinet agreed with several views put forward by historians on the need to establish a general policy on the declassification of historical documents currently classified as official secrets under the Official Secrets Act.

items.title: Classic Land Rover Defender associated with Cameron Highlands to get new lease of life as tourist vehicles
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Classic Land Rover Defender vehicles associated with Cameron Highlands could continue operating as tourist vehicles despite exceeding the usual 15-year age limit under a new Transport Ministry policy. In a statement, the ministry said the vehicles could be considered for use as Cameron Highlands Iconic Tourism Vehicles (KIPCH), provided they meet specified safety requirements, technical standards and licensing conditions. The ministry said the classic Land Rover Defenders were suited to Cameron Highlands’ hilly terrain and challenging routes, particularly for off-road tourism activities.

items.title: Deepavali: Higher Education Ministry allows online or hybrid classes from Nov 5 to 13
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) has allowed online or hybrid Teaching and Learning (PdP) sessions to be conducted at public higher education institutions from November 5 to 13 in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration on November 8. The ministry also extended its Deepavali greetings to all Hindu students, academic staff, ministry personnel and Malaysians. “May this Festival of Lights bring happiness, peace and prosperity to everyone,” MOHE said.

items.title: Selangor Immigration Dept repatriates 83,787 foreigners, collects RM42.6m in 17 months
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 30 — The Selangor Immigration Department (JIM) has successfully facilitated the repatriation of 83,787 foreign nationals under the Migrant Repatriation Programme (PRM) 2.0 from May 2023 to September 30. Selangor Immigration Department acting director, Mohmad Khusairi Kamarudin, said this achievement over the 17-month period represents the highest number of registrations and applications recorded compared to other states. “During the same period, the Selangor Immigration Department (JIM Selangor) also successfully collected over RM42.6 million, consisting of more than RM1.68 million in special pass fees and nearly RM41 million in compounds,” he said during a press conference at Selangor JIM headquarters here today.

items.title: Malaysian man, Vietnamese wife get 30 years for 173kg meth trafficking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The High Court today sentenced a couple to 30 years in prison after finding them guilty of trafficking 173kg of methamphetamine four years ago. “The court finds that the prosecution has successfully proven its case beyond reasonable doubt and finds both accused guilty and convicted on the charge,” she said. Deputy Public Prosecutor Goh Ai Rene sought a heavy sentence, citing the quantity of drugs involved at 172.74kg.

items.title: Domestic helper who punched autistic boy 23 times, recorded abuse jailed in Singapore
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Oct 30 — A 29-year-old Indonesian domestic helper has reportedly been sentenced to three years in jail for abusing a four-year-old autistic boy in her care, including punching him at least 23 times despite his attempts to protect himself. According to Singapore’s CNA , the woman, whose identity cannot be disclosed to protect the victims, also kicked the boy’s head twice in a separate incident and recorded videos of her employer’s children naked. Investigations subsequently uncovered four videos and two photographs showing the children naked in the toilet, with the woman having sent two videos and both photographs to her husband, CNA reported.

items.title: Home Ministry: Refugee registration card not a path to Malaysian citizenship, PR or permanent stay
items.summary: KDN said any employment access granted to DPP holders is temporary and limited, and subject to conditions and government approval. “DPP is also not an incentive or pull factor for new refugees to enter Malaysia. At the same time, KDN said lawful employment access would enable refugees to acquire skills, experience and verifiable employment records.

items.title: Cabinet approves UUCA amendments to lift curbs on students’ freedom, new law planned
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Cabinet today approved proposals to amend the existing Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA), particularly provisions seen as restricting students’ freedom of expression and association, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the Cabinet also agreed to develop a new law that would eventually replace the UUCA entirely within a reasonable timeframe. “In December, God-willing, the Higher Education Minister will table amendments to the existing UUCA,” he said.

items.title: Nadma advises public against panic buying ahead of north-east monsoon
items.summary: PUCHONG, Oct 30 — The public has been advised against panic buying or excessively stockpiling food amid concerns over the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), and instead to make preparations according to their respective needs. National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the spread of unverified information, particularly on social media, could trigger panic buying, potentially leading to other problems, including disruptions to the supply of goods. “Sometimes, panic buying creates another problem, not a Northeast Monsoon disaster, but a shortage of goods instead.

items.title: Melaka polls: Fire Dept conducts safety checks at nomination, vote-tallying centres
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — The Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) has inspected 28 nomination and official vote-tallying centres ahead of the 16th Melaka state election. Melaka JBPM director Mohd Zaidi Ma’at said the inspections were conducted at the request of the Election Commission (EC) to ensure that fire safety facilities at the centres were in good working order. “The inspections cover fire safety systems and emergency exits to ensure that safety at nomination and polling centres is given due attention.

items.title: Govt, parties to jointly monitor reform commitments under Bersatu CSA, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The development allocations provided for reforms under the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) will be monitored jointly by the government and the parties that signed the agreement, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said the monitoring would follow a mechanism established under the previous CSA, which involved joint assessments by both parties to determine whether the agreed commitments had been fulfilled. “The government intends to fulfil the commitments made under this CSA, particularly those involving institutional reforms.

items.title: Two charged with posting extremely offensive comments against Tuanku Muhriz on social media
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Two men pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to charges of creating and posting extremely offensive comments against Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, on social media in August. The accused, unemployed Abdullah Aidid Mochtar @ Ahmad Duta, 44, and graphic designer Ashadi Zul’izzi Zainal Abidin, 46, entered the plea after the charges were read before Judge Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad. Abdullah Aidid is accused of creating and initiating the transmission of extremely offensive communications with intent to offend through the TikTok account “rookiebenz_albenzauto” at 11.27pm on August 1, while Ashadi Zul’izzi is accused of the same act via the Threads account “razakahmad725” at 2.39pm on August 4.
